analogy.rationale: Succinimide antiepileptics (e.g., ethosuximide) act primarily by blocking T-type calcium channels, with some sodium channel and GABAergic modulation, so the closest transcriptional analogs are other antiepileptic/channel-blocking classes. Because these cells are not neuronal and express few of the relevant channels, the response is expected to be weak.
